question: A 10-week-old baby is brought for immunizations, but currently has a high fever and a bad cough. What should you do?

options.A: Refer the child straight to surgery for a diagnostic blood test
options.B: Defer the immunizations temporarily until the acute illness resolves
options.C: Administer all scheduled vaccines immediately regardless of the fever
options.D: Permanently ban the child from receiving any future vaccines

explanation: When a child is acutely sick with a high fever, it's wise to hold off (defer) the shots until they feel better so symptoms don't get confused. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h6)

question: Why is infection control extra important for open wounds treated out at sea?

options.A: Exposure to seawater and marine bacteria increases contamination risks.
options.B: Sunlight reflecting off water prevents wounds from closing naturally.
options.C: Shipboard water supplies are completely sterile and cause irritation.
options.D: Ocean air contains chemical toxins that dissolve human skin.

explanation: Spot on! Seawater and marine environments carry specific germs that can easily infect an open injury, making quick and clean wound care vital. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h4)

question: What is the surgical term for the complete removal of a fallopian tube?

options.A: Oophorectomy
options.B: Hysterectomy

question: Which serious lung condition is a major emergency for a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease?

options.A: Placental abruption
options.B: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.C: Acute chest syndrome
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Spot on! Acute chest syndrome involves lung infection and tissue damage, bringing chest pain and fever that needs fast medical care. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h2)

question: If a patient is severely dehydrated, which lab change are you most likely to see?

options.A: Elevated hematocrit due to decreased plasma volume
options.B: Decreased hemoglobin due to rapid red blood cell destruction
options.C: Elevated platelets due to bone marrow overstimulation
options.D: Decreased white blood cells due to immune exhaustion

explanation: When body water drops due to dehydration, the liquid plasma part of the blood shrinks. This makes the red blood cells look falsely concentrated, raising the hematocrit percentage. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why is a quiet environment important when conducting a neurological assessment?

options.A: To prevent the hospital equipment from malfunctioning
options.B: To keep the patient fast asleep throughout the examination
options.C: To ensure the lighting remains perfectly dim at all times
options.D: To accurately evaluate mental status, speech, and cranial nerves

explanation: Excessive background noise can distract the patient or mask subtle speech and hearing abnormalities. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h3)

question: Within how many hours must Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) be started to work effectively?

options.A: 24 days
options.B: 1 week
options.C: 72 hours
options.D: 1 month

explanation: Time is precious here! PEP needs to start as soon as possible, and ideally within 72 hours after a possible exposure, to stop the virus from taking root. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h4)

question: What should you do immediately if a patient says a warm compress feels like it is burning their skin?

options.A: Press the compress down harder to ensure even contact
options.B: Administer an oral pain medication and leave the compress on
options.C: Remove the compress immediately and inspect the skin
options.D: Wait five minutes to see if the skin adjusts to the heat

explanation: If a patient says it burns, take it off right away and check the skin. Never ignore a burn complaint! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T9#GNS221_U3_T9_h7)

question: When a patient fasts, how does the body keep blood sugar from dropping too low?

options.A: The liver stops all metabolic activity until the next meal
options.B: The pancreas releases extra insulin to store extra sugar
options.C: The muscles absorb all available glucose to build up fat stores
options.D: The pancreas releases glucagon to tell the liver to release stored sugar

explanation: Think of glucagon as the body's natural backup alarm! When food isn't coming in, glucagon tells the liver to share its stored glucose to keep your energy stable. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h1)

question: What is a common myth in reproductive health that gender-responsive nursing tries to fix?

options.A: Viewing reproductive health as exclusively a women's issue
options.B: Thinking men never experience reproductive concerns
options.C: Believing that contraceptives have no side effects
options.D: Assuming all patients prefer surgical interventions

explanation: You nailed it! Reproductive health concerns both men and women, and inclusive care brings everyone into the conversation. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is asphyxia treated as a sudden medical emergency rather than a chronic disease?

options.A: It can only be treated with long-term oral medications
options.B: It only happens inside hospital operating rooms
options.C: It happens because something abruptly stops breathing, needing instant help
options.D: It develops slowly over several months without symptoms

explanation: Asphyxia isn't a long-term illness; it's an urgent crisis where something blocks breathing right now, so every second counts for rescue! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T8#GNS123_U3_T8_h1)

question: A patient is prescribed a metered-dose inhaler without a spacer and complains that the medicine just hits their throat. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Instruct the patient to hold their breath for five minutes after inhaling
options.B: Call the doctor to change the prescription to a skin patch
options.C: Advise the patient to obtain and use a spacer device to improve drug delivery
options.D: Tell the patient to swallow the medicine instead of breathing it in

explanation: Spacers act as a holding chamber that slows down the spray, preventing medication from depositing in the mouth and throat instead of the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h4)

question: Two family members disagree sharply on whether to pursue aggressive treatment for a failing relative. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Facilitate a structured family meeting to let both parties voice concerns
options.B: Choose one family member at random to make all the final decisions
options.C: Tell the family members they are not allowed to visit anymore
options.D: Ignore the family conflict and follow only the primary doctor's orders

explanation: A structured meeting allows family members to express their viewpoints safely and helps the care team work toward consensus. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of creating a 'just culture' in the theatre workspace?

options.A: Making it safe to report mistakes openly without unfair abuse or fear
options.B: Firing any nurse who makes a small spelling error in the chart
options.C: Making sure the surgeon is the boss of every single nursing task
options.D: Throwing away all rules so everyone does as they please

explanation: A 'just culture' means we look at how the system failed rather than just blaming an individual, making it safe for everyone to speak up and learn from errors. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T12#GNS123_U5_T12_h6)

question: Due to physical immaturity, which medical complication is especially common in pregnant adolescents?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.B: Primary pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Chronic autoimmune thyroiditis
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Spot on! Young mothers face a higher risk of developing pregnancy-induced hypertension and preeclampsia compared to older women. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why do we usually avoid combined estrogen-progestin contraceptives right after childbirth?

options.A: They prevent the uterus from completing normal involution
options.B: They can decrease milk supply and increase blood clot risk
options.C: They cause permanent infertility in nursing mothers
options.D: They stop lochia discharge instantly

question: Which vitamin deficiency is the main cause of Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Niacin deficiency
options.B: Thiamine deficiency
options.C: Cobalamin deficiency
options.D: Ascorbic acid deficiency

explanation: Spot on! Korsakoff syndrome happens when the body lacks vitamin B1 (thiamine), which the brain really needs to keep memory working smoothly. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is a very common community myth about using contraceptives before having a first child?

options.A: It cures chronic malaria
options.B: It causes permanent sterility
options.C: It improves long-term eyesight
options.D: It increases household wealth

explanation: You got it! A widespread misconception is that starting family planning early will ruin a young woman's womb forever. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h4)

question: What is the main goal of the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: To restrict patient access to common over-the-counter drugs
options.B: To make safe and effective medicines affordable and available
options.C: To eliminate the need for international pharmaceutical trade
options.D: To promote expensive brand-name pharmaceuticals in hospitals

explanation: You got this! The core idea is simple: making sure everyday life-saving medicines remain cheap enough and within reach for everyone who needs them. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is family planning counseling so important before a mother is discharged from the postpartum ward?

options.A: Ovulation can occur before the first postpartum menstrual period returns
options.B: Sexual intercourse is strictly forbidden for a full year
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives are required to stop lochia flow
options.D: Pregnancy is impossible during the first six months postpartum

explanation: Many women are surprised to learn that an egg can be released (ovulation) before their monthly period ever comes back. Early advice helps them plan safely! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h9)

question: What is the primary purpose of giving intravenous fluids in Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: To raise blood pressure to normal levels
options.B: To shrink the size of the primary tumor
options.C: To flush out uric acid and protect the kidneys
options.D: To replace lost red blood cells

question: What is the main sign of ICT (Information and Communication Technology) addiction?

options.A: A temporary fascination with video games during school holidays
options.B: The physical inability to learn how to operate a personal computer
options.C: An allergic reaction to electromagnetic radiation from screens
options.D: Compulsive use of digital devices that interferes with daily life

explanation: You've got this! ICT addiction happens when device use gets out of hand, starting to affect your schoolwork, daily tasks, and relationships. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h1)

question: What is the first critical step a nurse must take when beginning a clinical assessment with an adolescent and their family?

options.A: Ban all family members from the hospital floor for the duration of the stay.
options.B: Prescribe routine vitamins without consulting the parents or the patient.
options.C: Explain confidentiality limits and conduct part of the interview with the teen alone.
options.D: Ask the teenager to sign a binding financial contract for their medical bills.

explanation: Private interview time allows teenagers to speak freely about sensitive topics, which improves assessment accuracy. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h7)

question: Why is the smoke that comes off tissues during laser or electrocautery surgery considered a health hazard?

options.A: It immediately trips the circuit breaker in theatre monitors
options.B: It instantly blinds anyone not wearing dark glasses
options.C: It can carry tiny live virus particles, tissue bits, and toxic gases
options.D: It stains the surgical gowns and patient skin permanently

explanation: When tissues are burned away by heat, they release a smoke plume into the air that carries microscopic debris and chemicals you definitely don't want to breathe in. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T12#GNS123_U5_T12_h3)

question: Which of these is a very common female-related cause of infertility?

options.A: Permanent enlargement of the prostate gland
options.B: Hyperactive sperm motility within the uterus
options.C: Complete absence of the pituitary hormone testosterone
options.D: Tubal blockages from previous pelvic infections

explanation: Past untreated infections (like PID) can leave scars or blockages in the fallopian tubes, stopping the egg and sperm from meeting. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why must a patient still do a biopsy after a routine screening test comes back positive?

options.A: A biopsy is necessary to cure the disease without surgery
options.B: Biopsies are required by law before any medication can be prescribed
options.C: Screening tests are always completely inaccurate for internal organs
options.D: Screening tests only suggest risk and cannot definitively diagnose cancer

explanation: Exactly! Screening tests only raise a red flag or show a risk. A biopsy (checking actual tissue cells) is the only way to say for sure that it's cancer. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T3#GNS321_U1_T3_h3)

question: What should you do if your patient's expected outcome is NOT met during evaluation?

options.A: Examine the data and revise the care plan to better address the patient's needs
options.B: Wait for the patient to figure out a new solution on their own
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately since the hospital stay is finished
options.D: Pretend the goal was met and document normal findings in the chart

explanation: Unmet goals aren't a failure—they're just a sign to put on your detective hat, figure out what's not working, and adjust your plan! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T7#GNS123_U4_T7_h6)

question: Why must you mention pending lab tests or investigations during a shift report?

options.C: So the incoming nurse can monitor preparation and follow up on results

question: Which annoying side effect is very common with ACE inhibitors and often makes patients switch to ARBs?

options.C: Tremors in both hands
options.D: A persistent dry cough

question: What is one of the best perks of using an electronic blood pressure machine over a manual one?

options.A: They are completely unaffected if the patient moves
options.B: They take very little training to use correctly
options.C: They give exact readings even during serious heart rhythm problems
options.D: They never need new batteries or servicing

question: What is the radioactive tracer most commonly used in a PET scan?

options.A: Iodinated contrast
options.B: Gadolinium chelate
options.C: Fluorodeoxyglucose
options.D: Barium sulfate

explanation: Great job! Fluorodeoxyglucose (often called FDG) is a form of sugar attached to a tiny radioactive tag, making it the perfect tracer to see which cells are gobbling up energy. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h2)

question: Why do we place absorbent material inside the secondary packaging of a medical specimen?

options.A: To cushion the glass tubes against heavy outside vibration
options.B: To soak up all the liquid if the primary tube breaks
options.C: To keep the biological specimen frozen during long flights
options.D: To absorb moisture from the humid clinic room air

question: What does informed consent require before a nurse or doctor performs a reproductive health procedure?

options.A: The hospital management approves the procedure during a board meeting
options.B: The client understands the risks, benefits, and alternatives and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The head of the family gives written permission on behalf of the client
options.D: The local community leader signs a clearance certificate

explanation: Informed consent is an ethical requirement ensuring the patient is fully aware and willing without coercion. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of circulatory overload during a blood transfusion?

options.A: Shortness of breath and crackles in the lungs
options.B: Sudden widespread hives and severe skin itching
options.C: High fever accompanied by uncontrollable shivering
options.D: Sharp pain radiating into the lower back area

question: Which route for measuring body temperature gives the closest reading to core body heat?

options.A: Axillary

question: How does the contrast dye help visualize the urinary structures during an IVP?

question: In the late stages of CJD, what does the term 'akinetic mutism' mean?

question: What is the main job of the parathyroid hormone (PTH)?

options.A: To stimulate the pancreas to release stored insulin

options.C: To lower blood calcium by moving it into the bones
options.D: To raise blood calcium levels when they drop too low

question: How do proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) help treat peptic ulcers?

options.A: By blocking the enzyme system responsible for acid secretion

options.C: By neutralizing stomach acid the moment it enters the gut

question: How do advocacy groups empower individuals who are going through rehabilitation?

options.B: By forcing them to rely exclusively on charitable handouts
options.C: By isolating them from mainstream political conversations

question: Why do nurses give anti-nausea (antiemetic) medications *before* chemotherapy starts, instead of waiting for nausea to begin?

question: Which type of exercise is best recommended for people with osteoarthritis?

question: What happens if glucometer test strips are left open to air and moisture for too long?

options.C: They change color to bright neon green
options.D: They become completely sterile to touch

question: During which phase of the nurse-patient relationship do you first meet the patient and build trust?

question: What must all rescuers do immediately before an AED delivers a shock?

question: What is the primary role of natural anticoagulants like antithrombin III?

options.A: To prevent unwanted clotting in healthy, uninjured blood vessels

options.C: To dissolve large clots that have already formed in the legs

explanation: Natural anticoagulants keep the clotting system in check so that blood does not form dangerous clots where there is no injury. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h6)

question: When should the nurse stop the repeating cycles of fluid instillation and drainage during a gastric lavage?

question: Who needs to be right there at the bedside when a very early preterm baby is delivered?

question: How does the pain of a duodenal ulcer typically behave compared to other stomach discomfort?

question: Right after a multiple birth, which complication should a nurse monitor for most closely?

question: Which children's condition often needs rectal washouts before surgery?

question: Where do water-soluble hormones usually find their receptors?

question: Why must nurses regularly check the vision of a patient who has a pituitary tumor?

question: Why does unequal household power make it harder for some women to get healthcare?

question: Why do some clinics continue to use outdated clinical practices instead of modern guidelines?

question: Which type of surgical sponge is the largest and best for major tummy (abdominal) surgeries?

options.D: Tonsil sponge

question: Why is poor nutrition (malnutrition) such a big problem during cancer treatment?

question: A woman mourns a close friend she lived with, but her family ignores her pain because they weren't blood relatives. What is this called?

question: A patient who just had major vulval surgery is crying and refuses to look at her wound. What is your best first response?

options.C: Mandatory
options.D: Measurable

explanation: In SMART planning, objectives must be measurable so the team can prove whether they achieved them or not. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: Which tiny blood vessels are mainly responsible for leaking fluid into the tissues when oedema starts?

options.A: Large veins
options.B: Arteriole valves
options.C: Capillaries
options.D: Lymphatic ducts

explanation: You've got it! Capillaries are the microscopic vessels where fluid normally slips back and forth between blood and tissue. When things go wrong, they leak extra fluid. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of having a surgical patient use an incentive spirometer?

options.A: To pump liquid medicine directly into the throat
options.B: To check the patient's blood pressure levels
options.C: To measure how loudly the patient can talk
options.D: To encourage deep breathing and prevent lung collapse

explanation: Incentive spirometry makes patients take deep, deliberate breaths, keeping their alveoli open and preventing postoperative atelectasis. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why are deep yellow and orange vegetables so good for your health?

options.A: It speeds up the absorption of glucose in the gut
options.B: It binds directly to cholesterol in the stomach
options.C: It acts as a precursor to vitamin A in the body
options.D: It serves as the main structural protein for cell walls

explanation: Great job! Beta-carotene is simply a plant pigment that your body turns into vitamin A, which keeps your eyes and immune system strong. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h1)

question: Why do some struggling families in crisis zones resort to early and forced marriage?

options.A: To comply with international nursing association guidelines
options.B: To gain immediate admission into secure university programs
options.C: As a desperate coping strategy to reduce household mouths to feed
options.D: To qualify for free public transportation out of the conflict zone

explanation: Severe economic hardship sometimes pushes desperate parents to marry off young daughters early, hoping to lessen their financial burden. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T11#GNS312_U4_T11_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of an incident report in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To provide permanent legal evidence for the patient's court case
options.B: To document safety events and improve institutional systems
options.C: To formally punish the specific nurse who made the mistake
options.D: To calculate the daily patient feeding and laundry costs

explanation: Incident reports aren't for witch hunts! They are learning tools to help the hospital spot recurring issues and make the ward safer for everyone. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h5)

question: When a patient is suspected of having an unsafe abortion, what should be the primary goal of your first nursing assessment?

options.A: Identifying life-threatening complications and vital sign instability
options.B: Reporting the patient's family members to hospital authorities
options.C: Collecting evidence for police investigation and legal prosecution
options.D: Determining the exact herbal concoction ingested by the patient

explanation: In an emergency, airway, breathing, circulation, and watching for heavy bleeding or sepsis always come first. A nurse's duty is to save the patient's life, not play detective! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h6)

question: What is the main job of the tiny bones (ossicles) inside your middle ear?

options.A: To amplify and transmit sound vibrations to the cochlea
options.B: To filter and warm incoming air before it reaches the lungs
options.C: To produce endolymph and maintain fluid pressure in the inner ear
options.D: To equalize air pressure between the ear canal and the throat

explanation: The malleus, incus, and stapes work together like a tiny lever system to boost the strength of sound waves as they travel from the air into the fluid-filled inner ear. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why should a nurse measure and document the centimeter depth marking of the endotracheal tube at the patient's lip?

options.A: To find out when the plastic material of the tube needs replacing
options.B: To calculate the exact amount of suction pressure needed daily
options.C: To determine how much air belongs inside the mechanical ventilator
options.D: To quickly notice if the tube slips out or pushes in too deep

explanation: Recording the depth mark allows any nurse to verify at a glance that the tube has not migrated out of position. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h6)

question: Why is checking blood sugar one of the first things to do when caring for an unresponsive patient?

options.A: Hypoglycemia is a metabolic cause of altered consciousness that can be quickly reversed
options.B: Glucose checks replace the need for a neurological exam
options.C: High blood sugar directly damages the brainstem within minutes
options.D: Diabetes mellitus is the primary cause of all neurological trauma

explanation: Spot on! Low blood sugar starves the brain of energy, causing unconsciousness that can fix itself almost instantly once glucose is given. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T5#GNS221_U3_T5_h1)

question: As women grow older, which health screenings become most important?

options.A: Ovulation tracking and fertility windows
options.B: Congenital anomaly prevention counseling
options.C: Cervical and breast cancer screenings
options.D: Testicular self-examination techniques

explanation: Spot on! Regular checks for cervical changes and breast health are vital preventative steps as women age. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the highest score a patient can get on the eye-opening part of the GCS?
explanation: Eye opening goes from 1 to 4. A score of 4 means the patient opens their eyes spontaneously without anyone touching or calling them! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T7#GNS222_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why is proper health care waste management strictly regulated in clinical settings?

options.A: To ensure the facility uses less electricity every month
options.B: To make hospital compounds look neat for visiting inspectors
options.C: To prevent the spread of infections and protect community health
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing office supplies

explanation: Strict rules are necessary because improperly managed medical waste can transmit dangerous diseases to staff, patients, and the public. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of primary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Stopping health problems before they ever start
options.B: Screening for early signs of hidden cancer
options.C: Rehabilitating patients after a major stroke
options.D: Treating advanced chronic diseases with surgery

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on risk reduction and health education to prevent a condition from developing in the first place. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h4)

question: You notice on your monthly report that many young clients are skipping their second injectable dose. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Stop ordering injectable contraceptives for the clinic entirely
options.B: Organize community education and strengthen client reminder systems
options.C: Refuse care to any client who misses an appointment date
options.D: Wait until the federal ministry sends a special investigation team

explanation: Wonderful clinical thinking! Spotting a trend like missed doses means we should step up our appointment reminders and patient counseling. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h7)
